primary_rules.claim: Pylon follows the attachment translation and actual rotation: r_p=r_i+Q*(r_p0-r_i0).
Engine force and intrinsic couple transfer to the attachment as F and M+arm cross F.
Engine axes rotate with the attachment. Inflow is evaluated at the engine, transformed into its axes, and the resulting force/couple transformed back.
Engine has no mass, drag area, volume or angular momentum; use a separate Weight for those properties.
Multiple engine rows may share one power index; each has its own normalized thrust vector carried by deformation.

source_section_compatibility: No constitutive incompatibility found. Concentrated engine nodal loads are jumps, not distributed interval loads; preserve source ends/couples and separate mass cache.

geometry_tangent.py:174-175,358-371 current mount geometry and engine inflow derivatives
necessary_validation: Independent finite-rotation/offset-pylon wrench targets; shared power at distinct attachments; global force and arbitrary-reference moment covariance.
No engine contamination of source distributed ends/couples or real-mass cache; no engine double counting in global aero/nodal forces.

Type1 and type2 disk power/torque/P-factor identities with actual rotated axes and current inflow; current/frozen influences; positive/negative radius preserves disk force while enabling/disabling jets.
Circulation and geometry derivative columns agree with complete physical residual stencils at two step sizes; detailed/compact residual agree; contexts restore.
Rigid and finite-section mounted equilibria retain force/moment balance and source operator identity on saved restore; unsupported dynamics and no-FlightCondition engine use remain rejected.
